synopsis: FAA AC 20-146A, Dynamic Seat Certification by Analysis, is regulator guidance dated 29 June 2018 and the booklet’s clearest published precedent for simulation as compliance evidence through a physical anchor plus virtual variants [f7618, f7619, f14665]. A baseline aircraft seat must pass physical dynamic tests, and its model must be validated against them using criteria agreed in advance; eligible modifications within the same seat family may then be substantiated by simulation [f14655, f14656]. Calibration is not validation, model-to-model agreement is insufficient, and extrapolation is limited to similar conditions; changes affecting load paths, failure mechanisms, materials or interfaces require new physical evidence [f7625, f7626, f14658, f14657]. The guidance uses 10% agreement criteria for several seat quantities and permits other model-specific criteria agreed with the authority, but these tolerances must not be transferred to off-road braking [f7777, f7778, f14668]. Its applicability to off-road automatic braking is unproven, the percentage of physical tests eliminated was not published, and the research did not verify broader FAA/EASA certification-by-analysis policy beyond this circular [f8087, f7853, f7634].
